title: Corrosion-Resistant Doubler and Drain Path Standard for the Aft Lower Shell

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Replacement of the aft lower shell inner doublers by titanium items with an open drain path, ending the recurring moisture entrapment that the earlier sealing standard only slowed down.

sections.reason: The interim sealing standard reduced but did not remove moisture entrapment in the aft lower shell joint land. Between 2017 and 2018, twenty-two aircraft were reported with surface corrosion on the inner doubler flange, four of them beyond the blend-out limit of the applicable repair scheme. The population at risk was the whole delivered fleet, because the driver is condensate running down the frame webs on short-sector operation rather than any single build feature. A permanent change was preferred to a further servicing instruction, which the fleet had already shown would not hold.
sections.description: The aluminium inner doublers at the longitudinal joints between stations C52 and C66 are replaced by titanium items, part number D5331121169495, of the same external geometry but with a machined relief along the lower flange that forms a continuous drain path to the existing bilge outlets. The joint angle D5331122892194 is replaced at the same time so that the two parts share a single fastener pattern, and the joint is refastened with rivets EN545167-02. Washers AGS334024-84 are retained at the drain grommet positions. Protective treatment follows the standard practice of ATA 51-20. The revised detail is on drawings D53311219246 and D53311251048. Access is through the aft cargo compartment in zones 131, 141 and 191, with the cargo lining and floor panels removed between the two frames at each joint.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 3.6 kg per aircraft, distributed symmetrically, with a centre-of-gravity shift below the reporting threshold. No electrical load change. The doubler is not interchangeable with the aluminium item because the fastener pattern and the flange relief differ, so a mixed installation across one joint is not permitted. The repeat detailed visual inspection of the joint land introduced with the interim standard is withdrawn once this standard is embodied. Illustrated parts content and the aft lower shell repair scheme both require re-issue, and the aft cargo lining removal task gains a step for the drain path check.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00243 in August 2019. Delivered aircraft are brought to standard through Service Bulletin CRN-53-1042, preceded on high-cycle aircraft by the inspection Service Bulletin CRN-53-1039. Embodiment takes about six days inside a scheduled C-check and kits are held as spares from the same reference.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, CG shift below 0.02 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00243, one extra shift absorbed in the aft fuselage join
